spots.name: Cox's Bazar
spots.description: Cox's Bazar is the beach capital of Bangladesh, with an almost unbroken sandy shoreline of roughly 120 km along the Bay of Bengal. Long walks at low tide, surf lessons, fresh seafood and huge sunsets make it the most popular seaside getaway in the country.
spots.history: The town is named after Captain Hiram Cox, a British East India Company officer who worked to resettle refugees in this area in the late 1790s. It grew from a small fishing and trading settlement into the country's main tourism hub.
spots.whyVisit:
- Walk one of the longest natural sea beaches in the world
- Watch the sun go down from Laboni or Kolatoli beach
- Day trips to Inani, Himchori and Maheshkhali island
- Fresh seafood and dried-fish markets
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is dry and sunny with calm seas. In the monsoon (June to September) the surf is rough and swimming is often restricted.
spots.hours: Beach open all day; lifeguards on duty in daylight
spots.entryFee: Free beach access (parking and activities are charged separately)

travelGuide.bus: AC and non-AC buses leave Dhaka from the Kamalapur, Sayedabad and Fakirapool areas, mostly in the evening and at night. Operators such as Green Line, S. Alam and Hanif run this route. Get off at the Cox's Bazar bus terminal or at your hotel's drop-off point; most hotels are on the Kolatoli-Laboni-Sugandha beach strip.
travelGuide.train: Intercity trains run from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar railway station (the line opened in 2022). Book through the Bangladesh Railway e-ticket site and check the current train names and timetable. From the station take a CNG or auto-rickshaw to the beach. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Biman Bangladesh, US-Bangla and other airlines fly Dhaka to Cox's Bazar Airport (CXB) in about one hour. The airport is a few kilometres from the main beach; take a CNG or arrange a hotel pickup.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG auto-rickshaws and tuk-tuks around town
- Rickshaws for short hops
- Jeeps and microbuses for the Marine Drive to Inani and Himchori
- Boats from the town ghat to Maheshkhali
travelGuide.distance: About 400 km by road from Dhaka
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 9 to 11 hours by bus; about 1 hour by air
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Cumilla, Feni, Chattogram, then the Chattogram-Cox's Bazar highway.

safetyTips: Swim only in lifeguard-marked zones and stay out of the sea when red flags are flying.
Book hotels well ahead for winter weekends and public holidays.
Agree the fare before hiring a CNG, jeep or boat.
Carry sunscreen and take your plastic waste with you.
Check tide times before visiting sea caves or driving on the sand.

spots.name: Saint Martin's Island
spots.description: Saint Martin's is the only coral island in Bangladesh, a small, palm-fringed island at the northeastern tip of the Bay of Bengal. Clear turquoise water, rocky coral shores and a quiet village life set it apart from the mainland beaches.
spots.history: Locally called Narikel Jinjira, or Coconut Island, it was settled by Arab traders and later by fishing families from Teknaf. The southern tip, Chhera Dwip, becomes a separate islet at high tide.
spots.whyVisit:
- Rare coral reefs and clear water
- Sunrise and sunset from the same shore
- Slow, car-free village life
- Fresh seafood and coconuts
spots.bestTimeNote: The sea is calm from November to February, which is also when passenger ships operate most reliably. Ships often stop in the monsoon.
spots.entryFee: Ship ticket and local fees apply; amounts vary by operator and season

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Teknaf (about 10 to 12 hours). Overnight services run from the Kamalapur and Sayedabad areas. Get off at Teknaf bus stand, then go to the jetty by CNG or rickshaw.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar, then a bus or microbus along the Marine Drive to Teknaf (about 2 to 3 hours). Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Cox's Bazar, then continue by road to Teknaf. There is no airport on the island.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Passenger ships and trawlers from Teknaf jetty (about 2 to 3 hours)
- On the island, everything is on foot or by cycle-rickshaw and van
travelGuide.distance: About 480 km from Dhaka to Teknaf, then about 40 km by sea
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 12 to 15 hours in total including the sea crossing
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Cox's Bazar, Teknaf jetty, then ship to Saint Martin's.
travelGuide.instructions: Access rules for the island, including visitor numbers and overnight stays, have changed in recent years. Check the current rules with the local administration before booking.

safetyTips: Confirm ship schedules and current visitor rules before you leave.
Do not pick up or buy coral, shells or sea turtle products.
Carry cash: there are few ATMs and signal can be weak.
Bring back all your rubbish; the island has limited waste handling.
Keep noise and lights down at night to protect nesting turtles.

spots.name: Sajek Valley
spots.description: Sajek Valley sits on a hill ridge at roughly 1,800 ft in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. In the monsoon and early autumn, clouds roll below the ridge and tribal cottages appear to float above them.
spots.history: Sajek is home to the Chakma, Tripura, Lushai and Pangkhua communities. The valley was opened to visitors in the 2010s after a road was built, and it has since become one of the most photographed places in the country.
spots.whyVisit:
- Sea of clouds at sunrise
- Traditional hill-people villages
- Konglak Para and Ruilui Para viewpoints
- Cool air and quiet nights
spots.bestTimeNote: July to October is best for clouds and green hills. Winter mornings are cold and clear, with good sunrise views.
spots.hours: Open all day; travel in daylight
spots.entryFee: No general entry fee; local security registration may apply

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Khagrachhari (about 7 to 8 hours), then a jeep (Chander Gari) via Dighinala to Sajek. Get off at Khagrachhari town and walk to the Chander Gari stand.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Chattogram or Cumilla, then a bus to Khagrachhari. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: The nearest commercial airport is Chattogram (CGP); from there travel by road to Khagrachhari.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Chander Gari (open jeep) from Khagrachhari, about 2 to 3 hours
- Vehicles travel from Dighinala in escorted convoys at fixed times; confirm the times locally
- Motorbike or walking inside the valley
travelGuide.distance: About 300 km from Dhaka to Khagrachhari, then about 65 km to Sajek
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Cumilla, Chattogram, Khagrachhari, Dighinala, Sajek.

safetyTips: Start early: convoy timings can leave you stranded if you miss them.
Carry your NID or passport for checkpoint registration.
Respect local customs and ask before photographing people.
Roads are steep and slippery in heavy rain; avoid night travel.
Bring warm clothes and a rain jacket.

spots.name: Nilachal and the Bandarban Hills
spots.description: Bandarban is the highest and wildest of the three hill districts, with cloud-level viewpoints such as Nilachal and Nilgiri, tall waterfalls and Bangladesh's highest peaks. It is the country's centre for trekking and hill-people culture.
spots.history: The district is home to Marma, Bawm, Tripura, Mro and other communities, and the Bohmong Chief's royal seat is at Bandarban town. The Golden Temple (Buddha Dhatu Jadi) sits on a hill just outside the town.
spots.whyVisit:
- Views over the Sangu river valley
- Boga Lake, Nafakhum and Shoilo Propat waterfalls
- Trekking towards Keokradong and Tajingdong
- Hill-people markets and food
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is dry and ideal for trekking. Monsoon roads can be slippery, but waterfalls are at their fullest.
spots.entryFee: Small entry fees at some viewpoints; guides and permits cost extra for treks

travelGuide.bus: Buses run from Dhaka to Bandarban town (about 9 to 10 hours) from the Sayedabad and Kamalapur areas. Get off at Bandarban bus stand and take a CNG to your hotel or jeep stand.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Chattogram, then a bus to Bandarban (about 3 hours). Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly to Chattogram (CGP) or Cox's Bazar (CXB), then continue by road.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Chander Gari (open jeep) to Nilgiri, Nilachal and other viewpoints
- CNG in town
- Local guides are needed for trekking routes
travelGuide.distance: About 330 km by road from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Cumilla, Chattogram, Bandarban.
travelGuide.instructions: Many trekking routes require a local guide and a permit from the district administration. Arrange these in Bandarban town before you set off.

safetyTips: Hire licensed local guides for treks; do not go alone.
Carry water, snacks and a torch.
Check the local security situation before travelling.
Buy tickets for jeeps and rooms in advance in peak season.
Do not litter in villages or on the trails.

spots.name: Kaptai Lake, Rangamati
spots.description: Kaptai Lake is the largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, and Rangamati town sits on its shores among forested islands. Boat trips reach the Hanging Bridge, Shuvolong waterfall, tribal villages and quiet coves.
spots.history: The lake was created in the early 1960s when the Kaptai Dam was built across the Karnaphuli river, submerging a large area of the valley. Rangamati was the seat of the Chakma Raja, and the Rajbari stands in the town.
spots.whyVisit:
- Boat rides across the lake
- Hanging Bridge over the water
- Tribal Cultural Institute and Rajbari
- Traditional weaving and handicrafts
spots.bestTimeNote: October to February is pleasant and clear. The monsoon is green but often wet and misty.
spots.hours: Boats run from about 8am to sunset
spots.entryFee: Boat hire is per boat; fees vary and are negotiable

travelGuide.bus: Buses run from Dhaka to Rangamati (about 7 to 8 hours) from the Kamalapur and Sayedabad areas. Get off at Rangamati bus stand and take a CNG to the boat ghat.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Chattogram, then a bus to Rangamati (about 2.5 hours). Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly to Chattogram (CGP) then continue by road (about 75 km).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Speedboats and engine boats on the lake
- CNG auto-rickshaws in town
travelGuide.distance: About 300 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Cumilla, Chattogram, Kaptai road, Rangamati.

safetyTips: Wear a life jacket on boats.
Agree on the route and price before boarding.
Carry a rain jacket in the monsoon.
Buy local textiles from cooperatives where possible.
Do not litter in the lake.

spots.name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
spots.description: Ratargul is one of the few freshwater swamp forests in the world. In the rainy season the water rises and you glide by boat between the trunks of submerged trees.
spots.history: The forest lies in Gowainghat upazila beside the Goain river and was declared a reserved forest. It has grown up over a flooded plain that is dry for part of the year.
spots.whyVisit:
- Paddle boats through flooded trees
- Birdwatching and quiet water
- A rare freshwater swamp habitat
- Easy day trip from Sylhet city
spots.bestTimeNote: Boat trips are best from June to October when the forest is flooded. In the dry season, the water is low and boats often cannot enter.
spots.entryFee: Small forest entry fee; boat hire is charged separately

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Sylhet (about 5 to 6 hours) and get off at Kadamtali or Sylhet city. From there, take a CNG to Fatehpur/Gowainghat.
travelGuide.train: Take an intercity train from Dhaka to Sylhet (about 7 hours), then a CNG or local bus towards Gowainghat. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Sylhet Osmani International Airport (ZYL) in about 45 minutes, then continue by CNG.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or bus from Sylhet to Fatehpur/Gowainghat (about 1 hour)
- Local boat from the forest edge (hire per boat)
travelGuide.distance: About 260 km from Dhaka to Sylhet, then about 26 km to Ratargul
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 7 to 8 hours in total by road
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Sylhet, Gowainghat, then the Ratargul boat point.

safetyTips: Wear a life jacket on boats.
Do not litter; the swamp is sensitive.
Avoid visiting after heavy storms.
Carry insect repellent and light rain gear.
Hire boats through official boatmen at the ghat.

spots.name: Jaflong
spots.description: Jaflong is a border area where the Piyain river spills out of the Meghalaya hills. Rocky riverbeds, tea gardens, stone-collecting boats and views of the Khasi hills make it a favourite day trip from Sylhet.
spots.history: The area is home to Khasi communities and has long been known for its stone and boulders, gathered from the river and carried by boat. Nearby Tamabil is one of the main land border crossings with India.
spots.whyVisit:
- Hills of Meghalaya across the river
- Boat rides on the Piyain
- Khasi village life
- Tea gardens and viewpoints nearby
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February has clear skies. In the monsoon the river is high and waterfalls appear on the hills.
spots.entryFee: Entry is free; boat hire is extra

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Sylhet, then a CNG or local bus to Jaflong (about 2 hours). Get off at Jaflong bazaar.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Sylhet, then continue by CNG or bus. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Sylhet Osmani International Airport (ZYL) and continue by road.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or microbus from Sylhet town (about 1.5 to 2 hours)
- Local boats on the river
travelGuide.distance: About 320 km from Dhaka, about 60 km from Sylhet
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 8 to 9 hours by road, 2 hours from Sylhet
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Sylhet, Gowainghat, Jaflong.
travelGuide.instructions: Jaflong is at an international border. Stay on the Bangladesh side, do not cross without proper documents, and follow the guidance of local police and border guards.

safetyTips: Do not cross into India without valid documents.
Avoid walking near river edges after rain.
Buy local snacks and betel-leaf specialities from village stalls.
Carry cash; card acceptance is limited.
Leave no rubbish on the riverbed.

spots.name: The Sundarbans
spots.description: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest on Earth, a maze of tidal rivers and creeks shared with India. It is home to the Royal Bengal tiger, spotted deer, saltwater crocodiles and hundreds of bird species.
spots.history: The Bangladesh Sundarbans was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997. The forest is named for the sundari tree, and local honey collectors and fishers have worked its waters for generations.
spots.whyVisit:
- Mangrove creeks by boat
- Chances to see deer, monkeys, crocodiles and birds
- Sunrise over the forest
- Traditional honey-collecting culture
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is cooler and easier for travel and wildlife viewing. Summer is hot and humid; cyclones are possible in the monsoon and early autumn.
spots.hours: Daylight hours; entry with a licensed operator
spots.entryFee: Forest Department entry and permit fees apply, plus boat and guide fees

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Khulna (about 5 to 8 hours via the Padma Bridge) and then to Mongla. Get off at Khulna Sheikh Russell bus stand, or continue to Mongla.
travelGuide.train: Take a train to Khulna or Jashore via the Padma Bridge rail link, then continue by road. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Jashore Airport (JSR), then travel by road to Khulna (about 2 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Licensed tour boats and launches from Khulna, Mongla or Harbaria
- Small local boats for creek excursions
- Karamjal, Katka and Hiron Point are the main tourist stops
travelGuide.distance: About 270 km to Khulna, then 45 to 100 km to forest entry points
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 8 to 10 hours by road, then a 2-to-3-day boat tour
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Padma Bridge, Khulna or Mongla, then the boat route into the forest.
travelGuide.instructions: Entry to the Sundarbans requires permits and a licensed operator. Book through a recognised tour company and follow forest rangers' directions at all times.

safetyTips: Never leave the boat or walk into the forest unescorted.
Book only licensed operators and follow park rules.
Bring sun protection, insect repellent and a rain jacket.
Do not feed wildlife and never litter.
Keep noise down to avoid disturbing animals.

spots.name: Kuakata
spots.description: Kuakata is known as the Daughter of the Sea (Sagar Kannya). It is one of the few places in Bangladesh where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the sea from the same beach.
spots.history: The name comes from a local word for a well (kua) dug by early Rakhine settlers. The Rakhine community still lives here and keeps a Buddhist temple and traditional crafts alive.
spots.whyVisit:
- Sunrise and sunset from one beach
- Wide beach and calm water
- Rakhine culture and Buddhist temple
- Nearby Gangamati forest and Fatra forest
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is dry. Monsoon brings storms and rough seas.
spots.entryFee: Free beach access

travelGuide.bus: Buses run from Dhaka (Gabtoli and Sayedabad areas) to Kuakata via the Padma Bridge (about 6 to 8 hours). Get off at Kuakata Sea Beach bus stand.
travelGuide.train: There is no train to Kuakata. Take a train to Khulna and continue by road, or use buses from Dhaka. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Barishal Airport (BZL), then travel by road to Kuakata (about 3.5 to 4 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG auto-rickshaws and easy bikes along the beach
- Motorbike taxis for short rides
travelGuide.distance: About 320 km by road from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Padma Bridge, Barishal, Patuakhali, Kalapara, Kuakata.

safetyTips: Book hotels early on weekends.
Take care in the surf; there are few lifeguards.
Visit the Buddhist temple respectfully.
Carry cash; ATMs are limited.
Try local seafood and dried fish.

spots.name: Paharpur Buddhist Vihara (Somapura Mahavihara)
spots.description: Paharpur holds the ruins of Somapura Mahavihara, once one of the greatest Buddhist monasteries south of the Himalayas. A vast square courtyard surrounds a towering cruciform temple, and its walls are decorated with terracotta plaques.
spots.history: The monastery was built in the late 8th century by King Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty and remained active for about 400 years. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
spots.whyVisit:
- One of the largest Buddhist monastic ruins in South Asia
- Hundreds of terracotta plaques showing daily life
- A museum with excavated artefacts
- Nearby Mahasthangarh and Kantajew
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is cool and comfortable for walking around the site. Summer is very hot; monsoon paths can be muddy.
spots.hours: Roughly 9am to 5pm daily with a weekly closure; confirm locally
spots.entryFee: Small ticket; foreign visitors pay a higher rate. Confirm at the gate

travelGuide.bus: Buses run from Dhaka (Kallyanpur and Gabtoli areas) to Naogaon or Joypurhat (about 6 to 7 hours). From there take a local bus or CNG to Paharpur.
travelGuide.train: Take an intercity train from Dhaka to Joypurhat or Jamalganj, then a CNG or bus to Paharpur. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: The nearest domestic airport is Saidpur (SPD) or Rajshahi (RJH); continue by road.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or auto-rickshaw from Naogaon, Joypurhat or Jamalganj
- Rickshaw vans around Badalgachhi
travelGuide.distance: About 270 to 300 km by road from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Bogura, Naogaon, Badalgachhi, Paharpur.

safetyTips: Wear a hat and carry water in warm months.
Do not climb on the ruins or touch the terracotta plaques.
Visit the on-site museum.
Start early to avoid midday heat.
Hire a local guide for the history.

spots.name: Sonargaon (Panam Nagar)
spots.description: Sonargaon was once the capital of medieval Bengal. Today its highlights are the crumbling merchant houses of Panam Nagar, the Goaldi Mosque and the Folk Art and Crafts Museum set in a tranquil garden.
spots.history: Sonargaon was a river port and regional capital from the 13th century. In the 19th century wealthy Hindu merchants built the row of townhouses that now stand along Panam Nagar's old street.
spots.whyVisit:
- Walk along a street of 19th-century merchant houses
- Folk Art and Crafts Museum
- Historic mosques and tombs
- Easy day trip from Dhaka
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is comfortable for walking. The rainy season can flood parts of the old town.
spots.hours: Roughly 9am to 5pm; the museum has its own timetable
spots.entryFee: Small ticket for Panam Nagar and the museum

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Gulistan or Sayedabad to Mograpara (about 1.5 to 2 hours). Get off at Mograpara chowrasta and take a CNG or rickshaw.
travelGuide.train: Trains are not the practical option; use a bus or a hired car.
travelGuide.air: Not applicable; Sonargaon is a day trip by road from Dhaka.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or auto-rickshaw from Mograpara
- Rickshaw around Panam Nagar
travelGuide.distance: About 27 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 1 to 2 hours depending on traffic
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Dhaka-Chattogram highway, Mograpara, Sonargaon.

safetyTips: Wear comfortable shoes for the old street.
Avoid traffic peaks on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway.
Do not climb on unstable ruins.
Carry water and sun protection.
Ask before photographing residents.

spots.name: Tanguar Haor
spots.description: Tanguar Haor is a huge wetland of lakes, marshes and villages in the northeast. In the rainy season it is a shimmering inland sea; in winter it hosts hundreds of thousands of migratory birds.
spots.history: Tanguar Haor was declared a Ramsar site in 2000 in recognition of its importance for waterbirds and fish. It supports the livelihoods of thousands of fishing families.
spots.whyVisit:
- Boat houses on open water
- Migratory birds in winter
- Sunrise and sunset over the haor
- Village life on stilts
spots.bestTimeNote: July to October is best for water-scape and boating. December to February is best for migratory birds.
spots.entryFee: Entry fees and boat hire vary; confirm before booking

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Sunamganj (about 6 to 7 hours) from the Sayedabad area. Get off in Sunamganj town and take a CNG or bus to Tahirpur.
travelGuide.train: Take a train to Sylhet, then continue by road to Sunamganj (about 2 hours). Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Sylhet (ZYL), then travel by road via Sunamganj (about 2.5 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or bus to Tahirpur
- Engine boats or boat houses from Tahirpur
- Local guides for bird watching
travelGuide.distance: About 300 km by road from Dhaka to Sunamganj
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Sylhet or Sunamganj, Tahirpur, then boat.

safetyTips: Wear a life jacket on boats.
Book boats through trusted operators.
Carry drinking water and snacks.
Do not disturb birds or nests.
Check weather: storms can rise quickly.

spots.name: Sreemangal Tea Gardens
spots.description: Sreemangal is the tea capital of Bangladesh, a region of rolling green estates, lemon and pineapple orchards and quiet forest trails. It is a restful base with birdwatching and village visits.
spots.history: Tea planting in Sylhet began in the mid-19th century under British planters. Sreemangal remains at the centre of the industry, with several large tea estates open to visitors.
spots.whyVisit:
- Walks through tea estates
- Seven-colour tea at a local tea cabin
- Lawachara National Park nearby
- Khasi and Manipuri villages
spots.bestTimeNote: October to March is dry and comfortable. Monsoon is green but wet; tea plucking is at its peak in the rainy months.
spots.hours: Tea estates are open in daylight; ask the manager for permission
spots.entryFee: Usually free; some estates ask for a small fee

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Sreemangal (about 4 to 5 hours). Get off at Sreemangal bus stand and take a CNG.
travelGuide.train: Take an intercity train from Dhaka to Sreemangal station (about 4 to 5 hours). Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Sylhet (ZYL), then take a bus or car to Sreemangal (about 2 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG and rickshaw in town
- Rickshaw vans or hired CNG for the tea estates
travelGuide.distance: About 190 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.travelTime: Around 4 to 5 hours by train or bus
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Bhairab, Sreemangal.

safetyTips: Ask permission before entering a tea estate.
Wear covered shoes; leeches are possible in the monsoon.
Buy tea directly from estates for the best price.
Respect workers' privacy when photographing.
Carry insect repellent.

spots.name: Lawachara National Park
spots.description: Lawachara is a protected semi-evergreen forest that is home to the endangered western hoolock gibbon, monkeys, and many birds. Well-marked trails run through the forest close to Sreemangal.
spots.history: The park was established in 1996 to protect one of the last areas of mixed tropical rain forest in the country. A Khasi village (punji) lies at the edge of the park.
spots.whyVisit:
- A chance to hear or see the hoolock gibbon
- Nature trails through forest
- Bird watching
- Visit to a Khasi village
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is easiest for walking; early morning is best for wildlife.
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket; guides are charged separately

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus or train from Dhaka to Sreemangal and continue by CNG to the park entrance (about 15 to 25 minutes).
travelGuide.train: Take an intercity train from Dhaka to Sreemangal. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Sylhet (ZYL) and continue by road via Sreemangal.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG from Sreemangal (about 8 km)
- Walking on marked trails
travelGuide.distance: About 200 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Sreemangal, Lawachara.

safetyTips: Hire a local guide from the ranger office.
Stay on marked trails.
Keep noise low to spot wildlife.
Avoid strong perfumes and bright clothes.
Never feed animals.

spots.name: Madhabkunda Waterfall
spots.description: Madhabkunda is one of the largest waterfalls in Bangladesh, plunging over a rocky cliff into a pool in the forested Barlekha hills. The spray, the forest and the crowds of bathers make it a lively weekend spot.
spots.history: The falls are considered sacred by local Hindus, who visit for festivals. They sit in a forested area that has been developed as a park.
spots.whyVisit:
- Tall waterfall with a wide pool
- Forest trails around the falls
- Nearby tea gardens
- A short day trip from Sreemangal
spots.bestTimeNote: June to October has the strongest flow. In the dry season, the falls can shrink to a trickle.
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Moulvibazar or Kulaura (about 5 to 6 hours), then a local bus or CNG to Madhabkunda.
travelGuide.train: Take a train from Dhaka to Kulaura or Sreemangal, then continue by road. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly to Sylhet (ZYL), then travel by road (about 2 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or hired car from Kulaura or Sreemangal
- Stairs and short trail to the pool
travelGuide.distance: About 240 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Sreemangal, Kulaura, Barlekha, Madhabkunda.

safetyTips: Do not swim in fast water or after heavy rain.
Wear shoes with grip; rocks are slippery.
Do not litter around the falls.
Visit on a weekday to avoid crowds.
Carry a change of clothes.

spots.name: Lalbagh Fort
spots.description: Lalbagh Fort is an unfinished Mughal-era fort in Old Dhaka, with a mosque, a tomb and a tidy garden. It is one of the calmest places in the old city.
spots.history: Construction began in 1678 under Prince Muhammad Azam, son of Emperor Aurangzeb, but stopped in 1684 when the governor Shaista Khan's daughter Pari Bibi died. Her tomb sits in the centre of the complex.
spots.whyVisit:
- Mughal architecture and gardens
- Pari Bibi's tomb and the fort museum
- A calm break in busy Old Dhaka
- Close to Ahsan Manzil and Sadarghat
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is best for a garden visit. Monsoon rain can make old paths wet.
spots.hours: Roughly 10am to 5pm; weekly closure applies, so confirm locally
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket

travelGuide.bus: Local buses go through Old Dhaka; take a bus to Azimpur or Lalbagh Road. From Gulistan, a rickshaw takes 15 to 20 minutes.
travelGuide.train: From Kamalapur station take a rickshaw or ride-share to Lalbagh (about 30 to 45 minutes).
travelGuide.air: From Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport take a taxi or ride-share (about 45 to 90 minutes).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- Ride-share and CNG
- Rickshaw in Old Dhaka lanes
- Walk from Lalbagh Road
travelGuide.distance: Within Dhaka
travelGuide.travelTime: Depends on traffic; allow 45 to 90 minutes from most parts of Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Head to Azimpur or Lalbagh Road via Nazimuddin Road.

safetyTips: Avoid peak-hour traffic.
Keep valuables secure in crowded lanes.
Dress modestly when visiting the mosque.
Combine with Ahsan Manzil and Sadarghat.
Watch your step on uneven brick paths.

spots.name: Sixty Dome Mosque (Shat Gombuj)
spots.description: Shat Gombuj Masjid is the largest medieval mosque in Bangladesh, with 77 domes and dozens of stone pillars set in a green landscape. It is the centrepiece of the historic mosque city of Bagerhat.
spots.history: The mosque was built in the 15th century by the Sufi saint and general Khan Jahan Ali, who founded a city here. The site was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
spots.whyVisit:
- Impressive brick architecture
- Khan Jahan Ali's tomb and Ghora Dighi pond
- Peaceful setting among lakes
- A perfect stop on the way to the Sundarbans
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is cool. Summers are hot; monsoon paths can be wet.
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka to Khulna, then a bus or CNG to Bagerhat (about 1 hour). Get off at Bagerhat bus stand.
travelGuide.train: Take a train to Khulna or Jashore, then continue by road. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Jashore (JSR), then travel by road (about 2 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or rickshaw from Bagerhat town
- Walking or cycling around the site
travelGuide.distance: About 275 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Padma Bridge, Mawa, Bagerhat.

safetyTips: Dress modestly and remove shoes when required.
Respect worshippers and prayer times.
Carry water and a hat.
Visit early to avoid crowds.
Do not climb on the ruins.

spots.name: Mainamati
spots.description: Mainamati is a ridge of Buddhist ruins near Cumilla, with Shalban Vihara, Kotila Mura and Charpatra Mura. It holds the remains of monasteries from the 7th to 12th centuries.
spots.history: The site was the centre of the Deva and Chandra dynasties. Excavations uncovered monasteries, temples and terracotta plaques, and a museum displays the finds.
spots.whyVisit:
- Well-preserved monastery plans
- Terracotta plaques and bronze artefacts
- Museum with ancient coins
- Easy day trip from Dhaka
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is comfortable. The rainy months can be muddy.
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka (Sayedabad or Gulistan) to Cumilla (about 2.5 to 3 hours). From there, take a CNG to Mainamati.
travelGuide.train: Take an intercity train from Dhaka to Cumilla station, then a CNG to the site. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Not applicable; road or rail is faster.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or auto-rickshaw from Cumilla town
- Walking between the sites
travelGuide.distance: About 100 km from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Dhaka-Chattogram highway, Cumilla, Mainamati.

safetyTips: Wear a hat and carry water.
Do not climb or touch the plaques.
Visit the museum.
Start early on hot days.
Ask the guide about the history.

spots.name: Kantajew Temple
spots.description: Kantajew (Kantaji) Temple is a three-storeyed terracotta temple, thought to be the most ornate in Bangladesh. Its walls are covered with intricate plaques of scenes from epics and village life.
spots.history: The temple was built in the early 18th century by Maharaja Pran Nath Roy of Dinajpur and completed by his son Ramnath. It is on Bangladesh's tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage.
spots.whyVisit:
- Remarkable terracotta relief work
- Traditional Bengali temple architecture
- Quiet setting near the river
- Combine with Dinajpur's rajbari
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February is cool and dry; summer is hot and dusty.
spots.entryFee: Small entry ticket

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka (Kallyanpur or Mohakhali) to Dinajpur (about 8 to 9 hours). From there, take a CNG or auto-rickshaw to Kantanagar.
travelGuide.train: Take Ekota or Drutajan Express from Dhaka to Dinajpur, then a CNG. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: Fly Dhaka to Saidpur (SPD), then travel by road (about 1.5 hours).
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG, auto-rickshaw or easy bike
- Rickshaw vans in Kantanagar
travelGuide.distance: About 410 km from Dhaka to Dinajpur, then about 20 km
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Bogura, Rangpur or Dinajpur, Kantanagar.

safetyTips: Do not touch the plaques.
Dress modestly and follow temple rules.
Carry water in warm months.
Visit in the morning for softer light.
Combine with other Dinajpur landmarks.

spots.name: Birishiri
spots.description: Birishiri is a border area in Durgapur with a pale white-clay hillside, the Someshwari river, and views of the Garo hills of Meghalaya. The blue-green water of the pond in the clay quarry is a highlight.
spots.history: The area is home to Garo, Hajong and Bengali communities and has long been known for its china clay. Nearby, the Cultural Academy shows Garo art and life.
spots.whyVisit:
- White clay hills and turquoise water
- Views of the Garo hills
- Garo culture and handicrafts
- Calm river scenery
spots.bestTimeNote: November to February has clear skies. In the monsoon, roads can be muddy and the clay area is slippery.
spots.entryFee: Usually free; local guides may ask a fee

travelGuide.bus: Take a bus from Dhaka (Mohakhali) to Durgapur or Netrokona (about 4 to 6 hours). From there, take a CNG or auto to Birishiri.
travelGuide.train: Take a train to Mymensingh, then a bus to Durgapur. Schedules, fares and access rules change, so confirm before you travel.
travelGuide.air: No commercial flights nearby; travel by road from Dhaka.
travelGuide.localTransport:
- CNG or auto-rickshaw from Durgapur
- Boat on the Someshwari river
travelGuide.distance: About 180 km by road from Dhaka
travelGuide.route: Dhaka, Mymensingh, Netrokona, Durgapur, Birishiri.
travelGuide.instructions: Birishiri is a border area. Follow local guidance, keep to the Bangladeshi side and do not cross without valid documents.

safetyTips: Do not cross the border.
Avoid the slippery clay slopes after rain.
Respect Garo customs.
Carry water and snacks.
Take your rubbish with you.
